properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by earlier excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River at Birdsprings.

* WHEN...Until 215 AM MST /315 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River near Birdsprings is
occurring. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1241 PM MST /141 PM MDT/, water levels on the Little Colorado
River at Winslow have fallen below Action Stage and will continue
to recede. Flooding will remain a threat downstream of Winslow in
Birdsprings. Water levels at Birdsprings are expected to peak
around 9 PM MST /10 PM MDT/, and begin to recede around 11 PM MST
/midnight MDT/.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 12:00pm MST /1:00pm MDT/ the stage was 15.99 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. Minor lowland
overflow on right bank at Winslow.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Birdsprings.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 2 at 12:24PM CDT until October 3 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Along the West Fork Big Blue River in Southeastern York
County in east central Nebraska and Northwestern Fillmore County in
south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1212 PM CDT, the gauge along the West Fork Big Blue River
north of Grafton was at 13.0 feet, which was 2.0 feet above minor
flood stage of 11.0 feet. As a result, fairly widespread flooding
of pastures and fields immediately adjacent to the river
continues, including downstream through the McCool Junction area
to the Seward County line. Based on trends over the last several
hours at the Grafton gauge, water levels appear to have crested
and have started a very slow, gradual drop that should continue
over the next few days. However, it now appears that the river
will likely remain above flood stage until at least sometime
Saturday, prompting this Warning to be extended out farther in
time.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
West Fork Big Blue River.
- Some locations that could experience flooding include...
McCool Junction, and rural areas along the West Fork Big Blue
River both upstream and downstream of McCool Junction.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
